asian-rare-earth-bukit-merah.whole: Asian Rare Earth was set up in 1979 to extract yttrium from monazite and began operating on 11 July 1982; it was owned 35% by Mitsubishi Chemical Industries, 35% by Beh Minerals, 20% by the state pilgrims' fund Tabung Haji and 10% by other Malaysian businessmen. In 1992 Supreme Court judges suspending a closure order said closure would bring hardship to the company and its 183 workers (Consumers' Association of Penang chronology). No output figures were found.

shell-basf-paulinia-pesticide-plant.whole: CIPER reported that Shell ran the Paulínia plant for about 25 years, making pesticides including aldrin, dieldrin and endrin until 1990 although Brazil had banned them in 1985, sold it in 1995 to American Cyanamid's Brazilian unit and BASF, and that BASF closed it in 2002. No figures on output or jobs were found.

metales-y-derivados-tijuana-lead.whole: The NAFTA environmental commission's factual record says Metales y Derivados, set up as a maquiladora in 1972 by San Diego's New Frontier Trading Corporation, produced refined lead and phosphorised copper from lead soils, cable sheathing, discarded batteries and scrap; a 1991 inspection found furnaces of up to 12,000 lb a day and crucibles of up to 60,000 lb a day, and the record gives no output figures. Estimates of waste left at the site differ: about 6,000 tonnes of lead slag (the submitters, 1998), 8,595 tonnes or 6,367 cubic metres of contaminated material (a 1999 report for Mexico's Profepa, which called the 6,000-tonne figure incorrect), and 7,265 cubic metres of hazardous waste, not counting material under the floor or in drums (commission study, 2001).
